This tag was retained without publishing a release after the dependency audit found newly published Rustls advisories. Version 0.5.1 includes these improvements and the Rustls patch.

Faster handling of large streamed events, a smaller executable, and more control over prompt caching. Existing configuration defaults, account affinity, and usage durability are preserved.

## Changes

- **Streaming efficiency.** Fragmented SSE lines are scanned once. A synthetic 4 MiB event delivered in 16 KiB chunks decoded in 1.875 ms, compared with 123.169 ms before. Ordinary small events and loopback proxy latency were essentially unchanged; provider generation speed is unaffected.
- **Smaller binary and dashboard downloads.** Build-time gzip embedding and removal of unused SQLite full-text/spatial modules reduced the executable by 4.96% in matching Linux builds. The ten dashboard text assets transfer 71.6% fewer bytes with gzip. ETags and conditional requests avoid downloading unchanged assets.
- **Prompt-cache controls and diagnostics.** Optional client/workspace key scopes, a namespace, and configurable handling of incompatible cache hints work across HTTP and native Codex WebSockets. Request details and structured logs show requested/applied policy and downgrade reasons. Caller keys and client isolation are preserved; session scope remains the default.
- **Less copying.** Request translation, response parsing, and continuation history avoid redundant copies and reduce time holding the routing lock.
- **Optional request limits.** Configure HTTP body sizes, concurrent requests, and aggregate decoded body bytes. Permits remain held through streaming and are released on completion, failure, or cancellation. Aggregate admission remains unlimited by default.
- **Faster rebuilds.** Docker caches dependencies separately from application/UI changes, and release builds cache Rust outputs by target.
- **Claude Code compatibility.** The default Claude Code identity now matches 2.1.299.

## Validation

The implementation passed 461 Rust tests, 50 dashboard tests, 30 Python tests, formatting, Clippy, and 12 isolated real-process usage checks. A production rollout preserved accounts, active session assignments, configuration, and usage history; health, readiness, compression, conditional caching, and database integrity checks passed.

See the [implementation report](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/main/docs/efficiency-2026-10-15.md) for measurement methods and limits, and the [configuration reference](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox#configuration) for the new options.
